name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+22 partisan lean makes this deeply Republican territory
Incumbent Mike Bost holds a roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic chance near 4%
No polls or expert ratings; the challenger runs a low-funded campaign
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's 22-point Republican lean, Bost's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and market pricing near 97% Republican leave no evidence of a competitive race, so the forecast stays at a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Bost or a sudden influx of outside spending against him would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 12th District in southern Illinois leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward the GOP. Mike Bost, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term and holds an overwhelming financial edge, having raised about $1.3 million compared with roughly $88,000 for Democratic challenger Julie Fortier. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Democratic side only about a 4 percent chance of winning.

With no polling to weigh and the challenger running a minimally funded campaign, the race rests on fundamentals, all of which favor the incumbent. Bost's incumbency, the district's strong Republican tilt, and his cash advantage make an upset highly unlikely. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican win, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
